questions.stem:
A botanist is conducting an experiment which studies the growth of plants.

The heights of the plants are measured on seven different days.

The following table shows the number of days, $d$, that the experiment has been running and the average height, $h\text{ cm}$, of the plants on each of those days.

| Number of days $(d)$ | $2$ | $5$ | $13$ | $24$ | $33$ | $37$ | $42$ |
|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| Average height $(h)$ | $10$ | $16$ | $30$ | $59$ | $76$ | $79$ | $82$ |

parts.label: a
parts.text:
The regression line of $h$ on $d$ for this data can be written in the form $h = ad + b$.

Find the value of $a$ and the value of $b$.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Write down the value of the Pearson’s product-moment correlation coefficient, $r$.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Use your regression line to estimate the average height of the plants when the experiment has been running for $20$ days.
parts.markscheme:
attempt to substitute $d = 20$ into their equation ***(M1)***

height $= 45.8683\ldots$

height $= 45.9$ (cm) ***A1***

questions.stem:
The following diagram shows two buildings situated on level ground.

From point P on the ground directly between the two buildings, the angle of elevation to the top of each building is $\theta$.

**diagram not to scale**

![Two buildings on level ground with point P between them. A is the top of the taller building (height h), B the top of the shorter one. PA = 150 m, PB = 90 m, AB = 154 m, and both angles of elevation at P are θ.](content/papers/img/2023-may-p2-tz2-q2.png)

The distance from point P to point A at the top of the taller building is $150$ metres.

The distance from point P to point B at the top of the shorter building is $90$ metres.

The distance between A and B is $154$ metres.

parts.label: a
parts.markscheme:
attempt to substitute into cosine rule ***(M1)***

$154^2 = 150^2 + 90^2 - 2(150)(90)\cos \text{A}\hat{\text{P}}\text{B}$ OR $\cos \text{A}\hat{\text{P}}\text{B} = \dfrac{150^2 + 90^2 - 154^2}{2(150)(90)}$ ***(A1)***

$\text{A}\hat{\text{P}}\text{B} = 75.2286\ldots^\circ$ OR $1.31298\ldots$ radians

$\text{A}\hat{\text{P}}\text{B} = 75.2^\circ$ OR $1.31$ radians ***A1***

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the height, $h$, of the taller building.
parts.markscheme:
valid approach to find $\theta$ ***(M1)***

$\theta = \dfrac{180^\circ - \text{A}\hat{\text{P}}\text{B}}{2}$ OR $\theta = \dfrac{180^\circ - 75.2286\ldots^\circ}{2} \ (= 52.3856\ldots)$ OR $\theta = \dfrac{\pi - 1.31298\ldots}{2} \ (= 0.914302\ldots)$

valid approach to express $h$ in terms of $\theta$ ***(M1)***

$\sin\theta = \dfrac{h}{150}$ OR $h = 150\sin 52.3856\ldots^\circ$

$h = 118.820\ldots$

$h = 119$ (m) ***A1***

questions.stem: The amount of a drug, in milligrams (mg), in a patient’s body can be modelled by the function $A(t) = 500e^{-kt}$, where $k$ is a positive constant and $t$ is the time in hours after the initial dose is given.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write down the amount of the drug in the patient’s body when $t = 0$.

parts.label: b
parts.intro: After three hours, the amount of the drug in the patient’s body has decreased to $280\text{ mg}$.

parts.label: c
parts.intro: The second dose is given $T$ hours after the initial dose, when the amount of the drug in the patient’s body is $140\text{ mg}$.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(i) Find $h^{-1}(x)$, the inverse of $h(x)$, and state its domain.

(ii) Write down the range of $h^{-1}(x)$.
parts.markscheme:
(i) swapping $x$ and $y$, or $h\left(h^{-1}(x)\right) = x$ ***(M1)***

$h^{-1}(x) = \dfrac{x^2 + 2}{4}$ ***A1***

recognizing range of $h$ is domain of $h^{-1}$ ***(M1)***

Domain: $x \geq 0$ ***A1***

(ii) range of $h^{-1}$ is $y \geq \dfrac{1}{2}$ ***A1***

parts.label: b
parts.text:
The graph of $h$ intersects the graph of $h^{-1}$ at two points.

Find the $x$-coordinates of these two points.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the area enclosed by the graph of $h$ and the graph of $h^{-1}$.
parts.markscheme:
attempt to form integral of the difference between $h(x)$ and their $h^{-1}$, using their limits from part (b) ***(M1)***

$\displaystyle\int_{0.585786\ldots}^{3.414213\ldots} \left(h(x) - h^{-1}(x)\right)\mathrm{d}x$ OR $\displaystyle\int_{0.585786\ldots}^{3.414213\ldots} \left(\sqrt{4x - 2} - \dfrac{x^2 + 2}{4}\right)\mathrm{d}x$ OR $6.5996632\ldots - 4.7140452\ldots$

$1.88561\ldots$

area $= 1.89$ ***A1***

parts.label: d
parts.markscheme:
attempt to use chain rule or power rule ***(M1)***

$h'(x) = 4 \cdot \dfrac{1}{2}(4x - 2)^{-\frac{1}{2}}$

$h'(x) = \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{4x - 2}}$ ***A1***

parts.label: e
parts.text: Find the value of $x$ for which the graph of $h$ and the graph of $h^{-1}$ have the same gradient.
parts.markscheme:
**EITHER**

$\left(h^{-1}\right)'(x) = \dfrac{x}{2}$ ***(A1)***

equating their $h'(x)$ to the derivative of their $h^{-1}(x)$ and attempting to solve for $x$ ***(M1)***

$\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{4x - 2}} = \dfrac{x}{2}$

**OR**

finding intersection of graphs of their derivatives ***(M2)***

**THEN**

$1.772776\ldots$

$x = 1.77$ ***A1***

questions.stem:
A weight suspended on a spring is pulled down and released, so that it moves up and down vertically.

The height, $H$ metres, of the base of the weight above the ground can be modelled by the function $H(t) = a\cos(7.8t) + b$, for $a,\ b \in \mathbb{R}$ and $0 \leq t \leq 10$, where $t$ is the time in seconds after the weight is released.

![A weight hanging on a spring above the ground; H is the height of its base above the ground.](content/papers/img/2023-may-p2-tz2-q8a.png)

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the period of the function.

parts.label: b
parts.intro:
The weight is released when its base is at a minimum height of $1$ metre above the ground, and it reaches a maximum height of $1.8$ metres above the ground. The graph of $H$ is shown in the following diagram.

![Graph of H against t for 0 ≤ t ≤ 10, oscillating between 1 and 1.8.](content/papers/img/2023-may-p2-tz2-q8b.png)
parts.markscheme:
**METHOD 1**

(i) amplitude $= \dfrac{\max - \min}{2}$ ***(M1)***

$\dfrac{1.8 - 1}{2}$

$a = -0.4$ ***A1***

(ii) $b = 1.4$ ***A1***

**METHOD 2**

attempt to form two simultaneous equations in $a$ and $b$ ***(M1)***

$H(0) = 1 \Rightarrow a + b = 1$, $\ H\left(\dfrac{\pi}{7.8}\right) = 1.8 \Rightarrow -a + b = 1.8$

$a = -0.4$, $b = 1.4$ ***A1A1***

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the number of times that the weight reaches its maximum height in the first five seconds of its motion.
parts.markscheme:
**EITHER**

$\dfrac{5}{\text{period}} = 6.207\ldots < 6\tfrac{1}{2}$ ***(A1)***

**OR**

consideration of number of maximums on graph in first 5 seconds ***(A1)***

**OR**

maximums when $t = 0.403,\ 1.21,\ 2.01,\ 2.82,\ 3.62,\ 4.43$ ***(A1)***

**THEN**

$6$ times ***A1***

parts.label: d
parts.text: Find the first time that the base of the weight reaches a height of $1.5$ metres.

parts.label: e
parts.intro: A camera is set to take a picture of the weight at a random time during the first five seconds of its motion.
parts.text: Find the probability that the height of the base of the weight is greater than $1.5$ metres at the time the picture is taken.
parts.markscheme:
finding second time height is $1.5$ metres ***(M1)***

$t = 0.571757\ldots$

in each period, height is greater than $1.5$ metres for $0.337978\ldots$ seconds ***(A1)***

> **Note:** Award ***(M1)(A1)*** for total time $2.02787\ldots$ seen.

multiplying their value by $6$ and dividing by $5$ ***(M1)***

$\dfrac{0.337978\ldots \times 6}{5}$ OR $\dfrac{2.02787\ldots}{5}$

$= 0.405574\ldots$

$\text{P}(\text{height is greater than } 1.5\text{ m}) = 0.406$ ***A1***
